summary.text: 备 means “prepare” or “ready” and is the standardized simplified form of 備. 備 is interpreted as a person carrying an arrow container, an image associated with readiness, though this construction does not establish the word’s earliest meaning.

formation.text: 備 is analyzed as 人 plus 𤰈: 人 depicts a person and 𤰈 is interpreted as arrows in a container, making the whole a carrying scene associated with readiness. The graph is also analyzed as a picture of a quiver. The proposed phonetic role for 𤰈 lacks an independently recovered component reading. 备 is the standardized simplified form of 備.

components.text: In one interpretation of 備, 人 depicts the person carrying the arrow container. Another analysis treats the whole graph as a quiver picture.

In 備, 𤰈 is interpreted as arrows in a container, or a quiver. It is also assigned a phonetic role, but the available evidence does not independently recover the pictured object's name or a reading for this component.

sound_limitation.text: No verified reading for 𤰈 is available to form a component–host pronunciation pair, and the pictured container's original name and pronunciation are unrecovered. The historical phonetic relation proposed for 𤰈 therefore cannot be checked from the supplied sound evidence.

history.text: 備 is reported in oracle-bone, bronze, and manuscript script categories, but the earliest appearance and sequence among these categories are unresolved. The curated glyph selection is empty, so no particular image can be described here.

The modern printed right-hand form 𤰇 is described as a change from seal-script 𤰈. Some bronze forms also change 𤰈’s lower part to 用, tentatively treated as a sound element; these reports do not establish a dated sequence.
The 1956 simplification scheme standardized 备 as corresponding to 備. 俻 is documented as a variant of 備, but the evidence does not establish that 备 was specifically derived from 俻.

uncertainties.text: The carrying-quiver interpretation may explain the graph’s association with readiness, but does not establish the spoken word’s earliest meaning. 備 is also reported as a written sign for 箙, “quiver,” in a bronze inscription. This is described as a whole-graph sound-based borrowing, but the pictured container’s original name and pronunciation are unrecovered, so the proposed sound match cannot be verified.

Reported meanings include prepared or complete, for use, cautious, equipment, and all or entirely. The cited examples do not establish a complete chronology or continuous development among these senses.

senses.text: Bronze uses are reported with glosses such as “equipped” or “complete” and “for use.” The carrying-quiver interpretation may help explain preparedness, but does not prove this was the word’s earliest spoken sense.

senses.period: received lexicographic tradition; date of spoken sense unresolved
senses.text: The received dictionary gloss includes “cautious” or “careful”; this does not establish the earliest spoken meaning.
Dictionary citations include uses glossed “all” or “entirely,” but do not establish when this sense arose or how it relates chronologically to preparation or completeness.
Later cited examples use 備 for equipment or facilities. The evidence does not establish that this meaning followed a particular earlier sense.

limitations.text: The earliest attested spoken sense is unresolved. Reported bronze contexts and received dictionary glosses do not provide a complete dated history of the meanings.
A bronze inscription reportedly reuses 備 as a written sign for 箙, “quiver.” The proposed sound-based borrowing does not verify that 箙 sounded like the pictured container’s unrecovered original name.

overview.text: 备 means “prepare” or “ready” and is the simplified form of 備. One interpretation of 備 shows a person carrying an arrow container, suggesting readiness; this picture does not prove the word’s earliest meaning.

components.text: In one interpretation of 備, 人 is the person carrying the arrow container.
In 備, 𤰈 is interpreted as the arrow container. Its proposed sound role cannot be verified from an independently recovered component reading.

relationships.text: In one interpretation of 備, 人 depicts the person in a carrying scene.
𤰈 is interpreted as the arrow container in the proposed carrying scene; another analysis treats the whole graph as a quiver picture.

A historical lexicographic analysis and another interpretation assign 𤰈 a sound role in 備. No independent historical pronunciation for 𤰈 was recovered, so the proposed relation cannot be tested through a verified component–host sound comparison.
